reviews.text: They're always happy to help you with your ammunition load.

I always receive clear and easy-to-understand explanations. They've even seen me outside of regular hours.

Not only the doctor, but the reception staff are also very polite.

I trust them completely.

My beloved cat was constipated, and I had to repeatedly manually dispose of her feces. She's not used to people, so each visit to the vet was stressful for her, but I finally found this hospital, where she was diagnosed with megacolon and underwent surgery immediately. She's recovering well after the surgery, her stomach is fine, and she's doing great!

I own a French Bulldog. At exactly four months old, his hind legs became paralyzed, and I took him to a nearby general hospital. The diagnosis was paralysis due to a congenital cervical vertebral malformation. They determined surgery was not feasible.

I was also told that the paralysis could worsen and he might have difficulty urinating and defecating. Desperate for a solution, I searched online and found this clinic, so I brought him in for an examination.

Dr. Aikawa said there was still a chance of recovery, so we performed surgery that same day. The surgery was successful, and now he's running around with boundless energy. I am truly grateful. Thank you.

He's recovering well after the surgery, and I highly recommend seeking treatment if you have a dog with similar symptoms.

During a health check-up ultrasound when our two Toy Poodles entered their senior years, biliary sludge was detected. At that time, the condition hadn't progressed to the point where surgery was necessary, so we opted for regular ultrasounds to monitor their condition. We were told that the medication, Ursodeoxycholic acid (Urso), was intended to slow the progression of symptoms, not to cure the condition, and we were asked whether or not to start the medication. We chose to administer it.

When the white cloudy mass in the gallbladder increased, the ultrasounds were changed from annual to semi-annual. When a white mass in the center of the gallbladder with granular dots around it was visible, surgery was discussed. However, since blood tests were normal at the time, we felt we couldn't take the risk of surgery and opted for further monitoring.

After several ultrasounds every three months, the white mass in the center of the gallbladder had visibly grown larger, and the granules had increased (resembling sliced ​​kiwi fruit). We then discussed surgery again, this time as a family, and received a detailed explanation.

Even if emergency surgery is performed after symptoms such as rupture appear, few children die during the operation. However, I heard that if the surgery is performed after symptoms appear, the risk of the condition worsening and death within 1-2 weeks after surgery increases.

After discussing it thoroughly as a family, we decided to have the gallbladder removed at the age of 13. The removed gallbladder was already enlarged, and I'm so glad we were able to treat it before it ruptured.

My beloved dog, Yamato (a video of him is posted on the website), dislocated his right front shoulder. Dr. Aikawa, one of only a few doctors in Japan with the necessary skills, performed the surgery. More than 10 years later, at 19 years old, Yamato still wants to go for walks, and although he occasionally stumbles, he walks and even trots.

Dr. Aikawa examines even elderly dogs carefully and treats them with genuine care. He is a truly wonderful doctor who is kind to both dogs and their owners. I am so grateful for his support throughout Yamato's life.

When my beloved cat fell ill, our regular vet couldn't determine the cause, so they referred us to this hospital because it had better facilities and could see our cat immediately. We went there feeling desperate, but Dr. Miyazaki, who was in charge, examined our cat very carefully and considered a treatment plan, and as a result, our cat recovered. Thank you so much. We would like to continue bringing our cat here regularly in the future.

My cat was extremely weak, wouldn't eat anything, and was constantly lying down and vomiting. I was worried and took her to the vet.
Dr. Miyazaki, who treated her, was incredibly kind and attentive, and after a week-long hospital stay, she was able to be discharged safely.
I'm so glad I found the best veterinarian I've ever met.
I want to continue bringing her here in the future.
Thank you for everything.

I have absolute trust in Dr. Aikawa.

He dedicated himself to saving my second son from a critical state of pancreatitis. Both my eldest and second sons had large amounts of bile sludge removed, and I felt completely at ease entrusting them with the surgery. I consider the fee to be the price for that peace of mind, and I'm prepared for the fact that if anything were to happen, Dr. Aikawa would have been the only one who could have done it.

Regarding treatment methods, the doctor sometimes asks the owner to decide after hearing several possibilities, which tests the owner's mindset, resolve, and tolerance. I believe it's about treating the animal not just as a pet, but as a member of the family.

When my beloved dog 🐩, who's like family to me, was in an emergency, I wondered where I should entrust him to. This hospital kept me in close contact with detailed updates on his condition and progress, and I was so glad I entrusted him to them! ✨ …

My dog ​​is a Chihuahua-Poodle mix. When he was a puppy, he had surgery for a fractured front leg and patellar luxation. I was referred to this hospital by my usual vet, and they responded quickly. Now he's 4 years old and perfectly healthy with no problems. I'm so grateful that I was able to get his care here so soon. The doctor is very reassuring.

I've had annual follow-up appointments since fracturing my femur four years ago.

I feel reassured by the thorough examinations I receive.
Thank you for explaining everything in such detail; it made me feel very at ease during my visit.

My Chihuahua is 16 years old and a senior dog.
At the age of 14, she developed a cervical disc herniation, which made it difficult for her to walk and left her bedridden. We were referred to this hospital by the head veterinarian, and he performed surgery.
Thanks to the doctor, his assistants, and the staff, she's happily going for walks and even running around just one month after the surgery.
I can't thank them enough.
She's still running around now.
Thanks to the doctor's advice, her weight has also decreased steadily, from 6.5 kg to 3.7 kg.
Thank you so much.

I had a consultation with Dr. Aikawa last month.

It was a reassuring hospital with a video presentation.

Thank you so much for the detailed explanation during my recent consultation.

Thank you also to Dr. Aikawa for your kind explanation of the treatment.

Thank you for accommodating my unreasonable requests.

I will come back for a follow-up examination.

Thank you again.

Updated May 16, 2026
Two years have passed since the surgery, and my dog ​​is now able to walk again. Considering that he was on the brink of never being able to walk again, this is a miraculous recovery. He's 15 years and 6 months old, so there's some age-related weakness in his legs and hips, but he's able to go for walks every day.
Another good thing about this hospital is that the billing is extremely fast, and the X-rays for follow-up examinations are inexpensive. Follow-up examinations always only cost a few thousand yen, and the bill is paid within 5 minutes of the examination ending. It's a truly excellent hospital.

==================================

I own a pug, and at 13 years old, he developed symptoms suggestive of a worsening herniated disc or spinal cord softening. I was referred to this hospital by my usual vet.

The head veterinarian provided a very expert, logical, and easy-to-understand explanation, detailing my dog's condition, what was needed, the potential consequences of doing nothing, and the probabilities of surgery. He provided all the necessary information for me to make an informed decision.

Because my dog ​​was elderly and a brachycephalic breed (pug), there were risks associated with general anesthesia. However, based on the information I received, I decided to proceed with the surgery.

Due to the urgent nature of the situation, the surgery was performed that very afternoon. It was successful, and my dog ​​recovered from anesthesia.

Although no spinal cord necrosis was confirmed after the surgery, the suspicion of myelomalacia had not been ruled out, so my dog ​​needed to be hospitalized for about 10 days for observation.

During hospitalization, the other veterinarians and nurses provided kind and meticulous care. I checked in with my dog ​​daily by phone, and he gradually recovered.

Post-surgery, paralysis in the lower body persisted, requiring manual bladder expression. I received thorough instructions on how to perform this at home. Because the possibility of spinal cord softening was extremely low, we were also given instructions on how to perform lower body rehabilitation at home.

All the other veterinarians, like the head veterinarian, explained the situation very clearly, and it was very clear what was necessary, what wasn't, and why.

Thanks to them, our dog was able to be discharged two weeks after the surgery. Although his hind legs were still completely immobile, he was able to urinate on his own, a miraculous recovery.

I'm so glad we chose Aikawa Animal Medical Center. I felt that the head veterinarian and all the staff were highly professional and that it was a very reassuring hospital.

Now, a month after the surgery, surprisingly, he has recovered to the point where he can walk two or three steps. I am truly grateful to this hospital.
